headline: High: CrewAI’s default shared workspace and broad egress create data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with Authelia’s OAuth/ForwardAuth outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout, so it can ingest Authelia-produced files or text if wired together. Authelia exposes OAuth2/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth outputs, which could be treated as trusted instructions by CrewAI in a shared workspace. No direct shared-channel proof exists, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into CrewAI prompts or task files
IF both agents share the same working directory without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Prefix all Authelia-derived text with non-executable markers
Disable automatic ingestion of task files
Add a manual review step before CrewAI consumes Authelia output

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI has broad network egress, reads the filesystem, and handles API keys; Authelia handles OAuth/OpenID flows and ForwardAuth. If Authelia artifacts or credentials are placed in CrewAI’s workspace, CrewAI can transmit them to model providers or tools. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default crew setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Authelia configuration, tokens, or logs are stored in CrewAI’s working directory
IF CrewAI tools or model providers receive those files as context
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Mount a read-only redacted input directory
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Restrict CrewAI tool access to non-sensitive paths
Use separate service accounts for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing behavior, while CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write files, and use broad egress. Even though Authelia is not marked writable, CrewAI can still contend over shared mutable resources such as files, configs, or downstream services. Lack of explicit locking makes conflict plausible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or downstream service
IF CrewAI tasks mutate files that Authelia also reads during auth flows
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and service endpoints
Serialize writes through a single operator-controlled queue
Disable CrewAI write access where not needed
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Use separate credentials per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing, shared-memory orchestration can treat upstream outputs as task inputs, and Authelia emits authentication/authorization decisions that are often authoritative. If CrewAI acts on those outputs without verification, a mistaken or manipulated auth result can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. This is a default-dangerous interaction because CrewAI is built to automate actions.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses Authelia decisions as authoritative task inputs
IF downstream CrewAI tools execute actions based on those decisions without human review
mitigations: Require explicit verification of Authelia outputs
Insert a human approval gate before action tools
Log and diff all auth-derived inputs
Limit CrewAI to read-only analysis for auth data
Add schema validation for Authelia-derived fields

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer that may process identity data, while CrewAI explicitly touches developer-passed crew data and can send it to model providers and tools. The profiles do not prove a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show a compliance-sensitive data flow with different handling surfaces and retention risks. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF identity or access logs from Authelia are passed into CrewAI tasks
IF CrewAI forwards those logs to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Minimize identity data sent into CrewAI
Redact logs before task submission
Set explicit retention limits for crew outputs
Review provider DPAs and residency settings
Keep auth data in a separate compliance boundary
